August 31, 2026 Credit: Adobe/mitarart The queue of vessels waiting to enter the Danube en route to Ukraine's river ports has grown to about 80 over the past five days, although the number of ships being allowed through the route is also gradually increasing, a shipper said on Monday. Russian attacks have effectively blocked Ukraine's main Black Sea ports, which once handled 90% of the country's grain exports, forcing Kyiv to divert cargo through Danube river ports with far lower capacity. Shipping agencies last week reported a growing backlog at the entrance to the Sulina Canal, the only Danube channel deep enough for vessels travelling to Ukraine's ports of Reni and Izmail from the Black Sea. Delays have been attributed to a shortage of pilots and the need to prioritise certain cargoes, including fuel shipments. However, traffic through the canal is starting to improve. While only about five vessels a day were entering last week, at least seven are expected to enter on Monday. "Since this morning, we have received pilots for seven vessels. Around noon, we expect more vessels to enter the canal, after pilots leave vessels which will head out to the open sea," said Katerina Kononenko from Avalon Shipping. "In theory, if we can move around 10 vessels into Sulina per day, we should be able to clear the queue of about 80 vessels," she added. Kononenko said it could take several weeks to reduce the queue to around 10 vessels. However, a rise in inbound traffic could create bottlenecks on departures, as more vessels will need to exit through the canal and undergo mandatory inspections, while the number of inspectors remains limited. MORE SHIPMENTS Officials at Ukrainian railway operator Ukrzaliznytsia said last week that exports via the Danube could increase, although operations continue to be hampered by vessel shortages and frequent air-raid alerts. The Odesa region, home to Reni and Izmail, has recorded 300 air-raid alerts since the start of August, lasting a combined 238 hours, according to a specialist monitoring service. Transport workers say entire days can pass without a single grain wagon being unloaded because of the alerts. Ukrzaliznytsia said it can transport 500,000 metric tons of grain a month to Izmail and Reni. Analyst data showed the volume of grain heading to Danube ports rose 35% over the week. https://www.digi24.ro/stiri/externe/rusi.text: Un schimb de prizonieri amplu, convenit între Rusia și Ucraina în cadrul negocierilor de miercuri de la Abu Dhabi, ar putea avea loc în două-trei săptămâni, a declarat generalul-locotenent rus Aleksandr Zorin, citat de agenția de știri rusă TASS, în timp ce Jared Kushner a anunțat planuri pentru noi întâlniri diplomatice la Moscova și Dublin, scrie TVPWorld . Zorin a afirmat că schimbul va implica peste 1.000 de prizonieri de fiecare parte, potrivit TASS. Kushner, ginerele președintelui american Donald Trump, a declarat miercuri că el și Steve Witkoff se vor deplasa joi la Moscova, înainte de a se întâlni cu președintele ucrainean Volodimir Zelenski la Dublin. El a descris discuțiile dintre Ucraina și Rusia de la Abu Dhabi drept un „prim pas pozitiv”. "Steve şi cu mine vom pleca mâine la Moscova pentru a ne întâlni cu preşedintele Putin, astfel încât să facem bilanţul a ceea ce s-a discutat astăzi şi să încercăm să facem progrese", a spus Jared Kushner la o conferinţă de presă. "Apoi, vom merge la Dublin pentru a ne întâlni cu preşedintele Zelenski, pentru a discuta cu el şi a aprofunda unele dintre ideile pe care le-am avansat", a adăugat emisarul şi ginerele preşedintelui american Donald Trump. În acest timp, şeful delegaţiei ruse la negocierile desfăşurate la Abu Dhabi, consilierul prezidenţial Vladimir Medinski, a spus că "dialogul va continua, fără îndoială", şi a anunţat că a fost convenit un mare schimb de prizonieri de război între Rusia şi Ucraina. El a susţinut că realizarea unei noi arhitecturi de securitate în Europa a fost tema centrală a discuţiilor de la Abu Dhabi. "Împreună cu partea americană, am făcut un schimb de opinii pe acest subiect. În anumite chestiuni am ajuns la o înţelegere comună, nu însă şi în altele. Iar această discuţie va continua, desigur. Lumea are nevoie de un sistem de securitate nou, modern, actualizat, un sistem echitabil, care să nu dezavantajeze nicio ţară anume", a explicat Medinski. Negociatorul rus a respins însă ideea unor discuţii între Moscova şi susţinătorii europeni ai Kievului, menţionând că "nu prea a înţeles rolul lor" şi nu este clar ce s-ar putea discuta cu aceştia în lipsa unor propuneri dinspre partea europeană. "Nu am primit nicio iniţiativă de pace, nicio propunere concretă din partea ţărilor europene, aşadar este complicat de văzut ce s-ar putea discuta" cu aliaţii europeni ai Ucrainei, a argumentat Medinski. De partea sa, unul dintre membrii delegaţiei ucrainene, David Arahamia, care este liderul grupului parlamentar al partidului Slujitorul Poporului, formaţiunea preşedintelui Zelenski, a declarat că observă un "impuls favorabil" în urma negocierilor de pace de la Abu Dhabi, care ar putea conduce la găsirea unei soluţii până la sfârşitul anului. Însă, contrar abordării Rusiei, oficialul ucrainean a apreciat că discuţiile ar trebui să fie multilaterale, nu trilaterale, adică să participe direct şi europenii la tratative. https://www.dw.com/en/nigeria-axe-wieldi.text: Skip to content Skip to main menu Skip to more DW sites https://p.dw.com/p/5POjW Prefer DW on Google Eyewitnesses say men armed with axes, clubs and machetes attacked supporters of opposition candidate Peter Obi on Thursday Image: Sunday Alamba/AP Photo/picture alliance Advertisement A group of armed men rushed a campaign event in Nigeria on Thursday, attacking journalists and supporters of opposition candidate Peter Obi at a political rally two months before the country's January 16, 2027, presidential election . Videos uploaded to social media captured the mid-morning incident, showing men armed with axes, clubs and machetes barging into an event center in Lagos, where they attacked supporters of Nigerian Democratic Congress (NDC) candidate Obi. Supporters, who vowed they would not be intimidated, blamed the attack on the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC). APC spokesman Felix Morka rejected the claim, citing a lack of evidence. The NDC has also accused the APC of being behind the forced cancellation of several of its campaign events, claiming the government of President Bola Tinubu is pressuring venue owners to turn them away. Here, too, the government has denied the accusations. Opposition NDC supporters battled thugs in the street after chasing them out of a campaign event Image: Sunday Alamba/AP Photo/picture alliance Fighting spills into the street Violence is a regular feature of Nigeria's elections and is often carried out by individuals colloquially referred to as "thugs." Eyewitnesses on Thursday said the attackers, "came into the hall, [and] broke all the entrance doors and the glass walls." "The NDC guys repelled them, chased them out of the hall into the road," one eyewitness added. Eyewitnesses said it took police more than an hour to arrive at the scene Image: Sunday Alamba/AP Photo/picture alliance After that, the two groups engaged in pitched street battles for over an hour before police arrived on the scene and began firing tear gas to disperse them. Security officials on the scene said they had not been on site to protect participants when the violence broke out because they had not been notified of the event. Journalist attacked, robbed A local journalist attacked in the melee described being hit with an axe as well as being punched and kicked before thugs made off with all of his equipment. "I tried to resist, so they started attacking me" said Sam Adebanjo of the online out TheCable . "I eventually yielded and surrendered the devices when one of them kept shouting, 'Leave the camera — do you want them to kill you?'" Peter Obi: 'I will not lose' — but can he deliver? To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video Oil-rich Nigeria, Africa's most populous country, ranked 112 out of 180 countries in the Reporters Without Borders 2026 World Press Freedom Index. January's election will pit President Bola Tinubu, who is seeking his second term in office: against Obi, who placed third in the country's 2023 election ; and Atiku Abubakar, who was runner-up in 2023. Abubakar is facing legal challenges to his candidacy and accuses Tinubu's government of trying to push him out of the way with lawfare, a charge the APC also denies.
